name: Lane Riggs

career.title: Management roles incl. General Manager-Process Engineering, Director-Supply and Optimization, VP-Refinery Planning and Economics, SVP-Crude, Feedstock Supply and Trading, SVP and EVP-Refining Operations
Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer
Chairman of the Board (in addition to CEO and President)

background_rationale: A chemical engineer who started as a refinery process engineer and rose through refining operations, engineering and supply roles to become COO and then CEO.

notable.summary: Valero's Diamond Green Diesel joint venture completed a sustainable aviation fuel project at its Port Arthur plant, allowing about half of its 470 million gallon annual renewable diesel capacity to be converted to SAF.
Reporting 2024 results, Riggs said 2024 was Valero's best year for personnel and process safety, as the company returned $4.3 billion to stockholders through buybacks and dividends.
Valero approved a plan to cease refining operations at its Benicia, California refinery by the end of April 2026 and recorded a $1.1 billion impairment on its California refineries.
Valero idled processing units and ceased all refining operations at the Benicia refinery, moving the site into decommissioning and redevelopment.

personal_story.hook: Lane Riggs started as a process engineer at a Texas Panhandle refinery in 1989; today he is Valero's chairman and CEO.
personal_story.summary: Riggs studied chemical engineering at the University of Oklahoma and began his career in 1989 as a process engineer at the McKee refinery in the Texas Panhandle. He later earned an MBA with an emphasis in finance and economics from West Texas A&M University. Over more than three decades he moved through process engineering, supply optimization, refinery planning, crude and feedstock trading and refining operations before becoming chief operating officer in 2018, CEO in mid-2023 and chairman at the end of 2024.
